q.t: The capital letter A has a line of symmetry that is:
q.e: Fold A down the middle from top to bottom and the two halves match.

q.t: The capital letter E has a line of symmetry that is:
q.e: Fold E across its middle arm and the top half lands on the bottom half.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter H have?
q.e: H folds both down the middle (vertical) and across the middle (horizontal).

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter N have?
q.e: Fold N any way and the slanting stroke goes the wrong way — the halves don’t match.

q.t: When you fold paper and cut out half a letter, the fold becomes the:
q.e: Both halves are cut together, so they match exactly on either side of the fold.

q.t: A firki (paper windmill) with 4 blades looks the same after every quarter turn. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
q.e: It looks the same at 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and full turn — 4 times in one full turn.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
q.e: A square looks the same after every quarter turn, and 4 quarter turns fill a circle.

q.t: Does looking the same after a FULL turn count as rotational symmetry?
o: No — every shape looks the same after a full turn
q.e: A full turn puts every shape back where it started, so it tells us nothing.

q.t: You fold a paper ONCE and cut a shape through both layers. How many matching pieces do you get?
q.e: One fold makes 2 layers, and the scissors cut both at once.

q.t: Which digit has BOTH a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
q.e: 8 folds onto itself both top-to-bottom and left-to-right. 3 only folds across the middle.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle?
q.e: It looks the same after 1/3 and 2/3 of a turn, and at the full turn — 3 times.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular hexagon?
q.e: It looks the same after every 1/6 of a turn — 6 times in a full turn.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of the capital letter S?
q.e: S looks the same after a half turn, so 2 times in a full turn.

q.t: The capital letter A has rotational symmetry of order:
q.e: A only looks the same after a full turn, so order 1 means no rotational symmetry.

q.t: You fold a paper TWICE (in half, then in half again) and cut. How many matching pieces?
q.e: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4.

q.t: Which letter has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
q.e: N looks the same after a half turn but cannot be folded onto itself.

q.t: Which letter has NEITHER kind of symmetry?
q.e: F cannot be folded or turned (less than a full turn) onto itself.

q.t: The digit 3 (in plain print) has:
o: Only a horizontal line of symmetry
Only a vertical line of symmetry
q.e: Fold 3 across the middle and the top bump lands on the bottom bump.

q.t: The smallest turn that brings a shape back to the same look is 1/4 of a turn. What is its order?
q.e: Repeat the 1/4 turn and it keeps working: 4 quarter turns fill the full turn.

q.t: Which letter can be cut out with a quarter fold (folded twice)?
q.e: A quarter fold always gives BOTH a vertical and a horizontal line. A, E and K have only one.

q.t: Turn the number 609 upside down (a half turn). What does it read?
q.e: The 6 lands where the 9 was and becomes a 9, the 9 becomes a 6, and 0 stays 0.

q.t: Which number looks the same after a half turn?
q.e: Turned upside down, 69 still reads 69. 66 becomes 99 and 99 becomes 66.

q.t: A design has symmetry at a quarter turn. You add one star. How many MORE stars must you add to keep the symmetry?
q.e: The star must also appear at the 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 turn positions.

q.t: A design has symmetry at a half turn (and not a quarter turn). You add one dot. How many MORE dots must you add?
q.e: One copy on the opposite side of the centre — the place the dot moves to after a half turn.

q.t: Which letter has BOTH a line of symmetry and rotational symmetry?
q.e: H folds onto itself and also looks the same after a half turn.

q.t: The smallest turn that brings a shape back to the same look is 1/3 of a turn. What is its order?
q.e: Three turns of 1/3 fill the whole circle.

q.t: Which statement is TRUE?
o: A shape can have rotational symmetry without any line of symmetry
Every shape with a line of symmetry also has rotational symmetry
Rotational symmetry needs a full turn
q.e: N is an example: it turns onto itself but cannot be folded onto itself.

q.t: A carved block is stamped four times round a centre, each a quarter turn from the last. What is the order of rotational symmetry of the print?
q.e: A quarter turn moves each stamp onto the next, so the print matches itself 4 times in a turn.

q.t: The word MOM, written in capitals, has:
q.e: A mirror down the middle of the O swaps the two Ms and keeps the O. M has no horizontal fold.

q.t: Which number looks the same in a mirror stood upright down its middle (plain digits)?
q.e: 1 and 0 are symmetric digits, and 101 reads the same from both ends. A 2 or a 6 flips the wrong way.

q.t: What is the SMALLEST turn that makes a square look the same again?
q.e: A square matches itself after every quarter turn, and nothing smaller works.

q.t: A design has rotational symmetry of order 6. What is the smallest turn that makes it look the same?
q.e: Order 6 means 6 equal turns fill the circle, so each is 1/6.

q.t: A firki has 3 identical blades, equally spaced. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
q.e: A third of a turn moves each blade onto the next one.

q.t: A pattern must have order 4. A child places 2 red dots on it. How many red dots must the finished pattern have?
q.e: Each dot needs copies at the 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 positions — 4 of each, so 2 × 4 = 8.

q.t: Which number looks the same after a half turn?
q.e: Turn 8698 upside down: the order reverses and 6 and 9 swap, giving 8698 again.

q.t: Which word has a HORIZONTAL line of symmetry through its middle?
q.e: B, O and X each fold top onto bottom. M, T, Y, C and A do not.

q.t: ‘If a shape looks the same after a 1/4 turn, it also looks the same after a 1/2 turn.’ This is:
q.e: A 1/2 turn is just two 1/4 turns, and each one keeps the shape the same.

q.t: A shape looks the same after a 1/2 turn but NOT after a 1/4 turn. What is its order?
q.e: The smallest turn that works is 1/2, and two halves fill the circle.

q.t: A rangoli has 8 identical petals, equally spaced round the centre. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
q.e: Each 1/8 turn moves every petal onto the next one.

q.t: Which is TRUE about the letters A and N?
o: A has only reflection symmetry; N has only rotational symmetry
A has only rotational symmetry; N has only reflection symmetry
q.e: A folds down the middle but doesn’t turn onto itself; N turns (half turn) but doesn’t fold.
